claims.text: The condition system carries a probability primitive — <comp>rand</comp> evaluates Math.random()*id <= qty — and the one authored use in the world data is a flat 50% random-encounter roll on an aggro spawn.
claims.quote: 112_Mobile_NodeData.bin:117 `<property>1,3,<xml><wave><enemy><id>1</id><qty>3</qty></enemy><enemy><id>3</id><qty>2</qty></enemy></wave></xml></property>` :118 `<condition><has><id>100</id><qty>50</qty><comp>rand</comp></has></condition>`. StatsManager.as:4222 `if(comparison == "rand") { return Math.random() * id <= val; }` — so id=100, qty=50 is a 50% roll; the default comparison elsewhere is "gte" (StatsManager.as:4171-4177).
claims.lane_impact: L4 enemies-ai blocker ④ + L1 world-exploration. This is spawn PROBABILITY, not aggro radius or leash distance — neither of which is in this blob, and I claim nothing about them. But it is the first authored encounter-rate number in the corpus, and the primitive generalises: any <condition> in nodedata, questdata or uidata can be made probabilistic by the same three tags.

verdicts.reason: HOLDS on substance and the string is verbatim at :1487 (resname 512), with zero corpus hits for 'third of your maximum'. I found the implementation and it confirms the fractional cap exactly — ScreenTransition.as:293-298, `case ACTION_REST: if(getPlayerStats(STAT_AP) < getPlayerStats(STAT_MAXAP) / 3) { setStat(STAT_AP, getPlayerStats(STAT_MAXAP) / 3); } fullHealth();`, reached from InteractUI.as:800 `startClose(ScreenTransition.ACTION_REST)` on the 'innrest' action. Not a refutation: the claim's own words ('AP only up to a third of your maximum', 'a hard fractional ceiling') are accurate.

Projectile.GRAVITY = 3 (px/frame^2), applied as velY += GRAVITY every update. EnemyArcher.fireArrow() fires from (mcs.x, mcs.y-60) at a target sampled at (target.mcs.x, target.mcs.y-60), solving a fixed-45-degree-ish ballistic: velA = sqrt(GRAVITY*|dx|/0.866), velXa = velA*0.866, t = |dx|/velXa, velYa = (dy - 0.5*GRAVITY*t*t)/t, sign-flipped when firing left, then a uniform aim jitter velYa += Math.random()*8 - 4. Above level 50 a coin flip sets Damage.LAUNCH_KNOCKDOWN on the arrow. EnemyGoblinThrower uses the identical solve; EnemyKanjiGuardian divides by 0.866/3 for a flatter arc.

new_findings.text: Skills 1500 and 1501 are not merely unnamed enemy-only entries — they are two additional STANCES. EnemyElite.init dispatches getMastery(1500) > 0 to setStance(REVERSED_STANCE) and getMastery(1501) > 0 to setStance(DUAL_STANCE), with the same dispatch in EnemyPlayer and FriendlyElite, and the build ships dedicated animation payloads for both. The shipped game therefore has FIVE stances (light, balanced, heavy, reversed, dual), not three. Carriers in npcdata: 1500 -> Aboshi (:3662) and Magoichi (:3898); 1501 -> Gojo Takamori (:3934 and :3956).

new_findings.text: The crit proc rule is HELD and it is DETERMINISTIC, not a chance roll. MCSPlayer.getDamage() applies the crit exactly when reload == maxreload, i.e. when the Focus/reload bar is completely full: 1.5x maxDamage in LIGHT_STANCE, 1.2x in every other stance, plus the flat gear stat STAT_CRITICALDMG (StatsManager.as:258 = id 204). There is no random term anywhere in the crit branch.
new_findings.build: android v0.682 (skilldata byte-identical to web v0.717; web longplay cooldowns reproduce from this codepath)
new_findings.ledger_text: ⑤ crit **proc** rule (chance vs deterministic) — entirely absent.
new_findings.lane_impact: L2 skills-meters blocker ⑤ CLOSED and L5 combat-core blocker ② ('crit 1.3 vs 3 final') answered. Also kills REBUILD_READINESS.md:152-153's ruling to 'Keep CRIT_MULT=1.3' — the real multipliers are 1.5x Light / 1.2x other. And it welds crit to the Focus meter: crit is not a separate system, it is the payoff for a full reload bar, which finally explains combat-core blocker ⑤ 'Focus/crit gating rule'.

new_findings.text: The on-screen 'Critical Hit' label is a pure function of the reload bar being at 100%: BattleUI.updateReload sets crittext.visible = percentage >= 1 && reloadbar.visible, and the text is LangManager.getString(175) = 'Critical Hit'. This is the HUD half of the crit rule and gives a cheap A1 verification target for a future frame pass.
new_findings.lane_impact: L8 ui-hud — the crit indicator is a discrete label above the reload bar, not a floating popup, and it appears the instant the bar fills rather than on hit. L2 skills-meters corroboration for NF-1.

new_findings.text: The shipped build contradicts itself on crit. InventoryUI's gear-comparison panel sets critModifier = 1.2 for LIGHT stance and 1.5 for balanced and heavy — the exact inverse of the simulation's Light-1.5 / non-Light-1.2 at MCSPlayer.as:3217-3221. The 'critical dmg: min - max (stance)' readout at InventoryUI.as:2087 therefore misreports crit damage in at least one stance.
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 combat-core must port the SIM values (MCSPlayer), not the preview values. L3 items-equipment: any 1:1 recreation of the (EQ:n) comparison UX inherits an OG bug — worth reproducing deliberately and labelling, or fixing and labelling, but not silently averaging.

new_findings.text: The stance-mastery term in both the reach and damage formulas is the 1-10 skilldata <value>, not a 0-100 figure. StatsManager.as:1834 passes getStat(1000/1001/1002) into MCSPlayer.initPlayer as lightMastery/balancedMastery/heavyMastery; getStatType routes ids 1000-1999 to SKILL and getStat returns skillStat.getValue(); and MCSPlayer.as:3166-3184 gates Launch/Deflect/AirCombo/Stab on `mastery >= 3 / >= 4 / >= 5`, thresholds only meaningful on a 1-10 ladder. InventoryUI.as:1941-1965 recomputes the identical coefficients from the same getStat calls.
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 combat-core — the reach and damage coefficients are now portable as numbers, no INFERRED label needed. Consequence: Balanced reach spans only x1.005..x1.05 and Heavy x0.505..x0.55, so the hard floor of 100 at MCSPlayer.as:3053-3055 is load-bearing for most of the game, not an edge case. It also unlocks the per-mastery TECHNIQUE ladder (Launch at 3, Deflect at 4, AirCombo/Launch/Stab at 5) which no claim in the packet carries.

new_findings.text: The per-stance DAMAGE multipliers are in the source and no claim in the packet mentions them. Light x(0.5 + 0.005*mastery), Balanced x(1 + 0.005*mastery), and Heavy / Dual / Reversed a FLAT x1.5 with no mastery term. baseDamage itself is minDamage + Math.random()*damageRange. This is the exact mirror of the reach formula: Light buys reach and pays damage.
new_findings.ledger_text: - **Ready:** gesture→attack map; damage formula ((ATK+Wpn)×stance, crit 1.3×, Heavy def ×0.8); blade-path-with-reach model; combo rules; part-based weak points (shielder legs, undead heads).
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 combat-core — the '×stance' term in the ledger's damage formula is now an exact three-way expression, and Heavy/Dual/Reversed damage does NOT scale with mastery at all, which changes the whole build-progression story. L4 enemies-ai: elite NPCs in REVERSED/DUAL stance get the flat 1.5x.

new_findings.text: getDefense() returns defense * 0.8 in HEAVY_STANCE and defense unmodified in every other stance — the source line behind the ledger's 'Heavy def x0.8'. Confirmed a second time by InventoryUI.as:1964 setting defModifier = 0.8 for heavy in the gear-comparison panel.
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 combat-core — the ledger already carries 'Heavy def x0.8' as Ready but had no source line; this grounds it and shows Dual/Reversed do NOT take the penalty despite sharing Heavy's 1.5x damage.

new_findings.text: The Focus/reload drain is stance-scaled, and landing a crit costs the entire bar. deductReloadBar() first zeroes a full bar, then subtracts slashUsage/2 in Light, slashUsage in Balanced and Reversed, and slashUsage*1.5 in Heavy and Dual. So Light rebuilds Focus twice as fast per slash as Balanced and three times as fast as Heavy — and every crit resets the meter to zero.
new_findings.lane_impact: L2 skills-meters — completes the packet's focus-is-the-reload-meter claim, which only carried the flat slashusage. L5 combat-core — this is the actual crit economy: Light crits often for 1.5x, Heavy crits rarely for 1.2x, and that tension is the stance meta.

new_findings.text: The Focus bar's displayed fill is not reload/maxreload. bonusReload() pushes the bar with updateReload((this.reload - 24) / (this.maxreload - 24)), so the bar maps [24, maxreload] onto [0,1] and the first 24 frames of charge are invisible. bonusReload also grants a flat +6 reload, clamped to maxreload.
new_findings.lane_impact: L8 ui-hud and L6 art-anim-audio-feel — a rebuild that maps [0, maxreload] onto the bar will feel wrong even with every number right, because the OG hides the first 24 frames. This is exactly the 'dynamic HUD feel' the ledger's :235 blocker ② says is uncatalogued.

new_findings.text: The Dragon Dance INPUT is fully held in a 650-line UI class nobody in this packet opened. DragonDanceUI builds an eight-node ring (node0..node7) labelled with the eight trigrams in two arrangements — Earlier Heaven ['sky','wind','water','mountain','earth','thunder','fire','lake'] and Later Heaven ['fire','earth','lake','sky','water','mountain','thunder','wind']. The player's input is a DIGIT STRING of clicked node indices. Earlier Heaven completes on a 4-length sequence containing nodes 1, 2, 4 and 6, which promotes the ring to Later Heaven. Validation is a string equality against the target object's sequence. The Kanji statue is Obj_DragonDanceStatue, whose Later-Heaven target sequence is drawn from five fixed permutations by a node-seeded deterministic RNG.
new_findings.ledger_text: ④ Dragon Dance **input** + Kanji-statue bonus.
new_findings.lane_impact: L11 meta+rebirth blocker ④ largely CLOSED. Supporting objects also recovered: Obj_DragonDancePath.as, Obj_DragonDanceLoot.as, DragonDanceInteractiveStageObject.as, Obj_HiddenTemple.as and shs3_android_fla/dragondancewords_212.as (the kanji word clip, symbol1534). Each node click also plays a POSE animation on the player character (MCSActor.POSE4 etc.) gated on canChangeStance(), so the dance is physically performed — an L6 art-anim requirement nobody has recorded. Refutes skilldata/input-field-empty's conclusion that blocker ④'s most likely home was eliminated.

new_findings.text: WEB v0.717's stance model is an explicit reach-vs-damage inversion, and both halves use the same mastery coefficients. REACH: Light base x1.4, Balanced base x(1 + 0.02*mastery), Heavy base x(0.5 + 0.04*mastery) floored at 100, Dual base x1 floored at 100, Reversed base x1.4. DAMAGE: Light x(0.5 + 0.04*mastery), Balanced x(1 + 0.02*mastery), Heavy/Dual/Reversed x1.4. So Light = long reach / low damage and Heavy = short reach / high damage, with mastery moving the weak axis. The ANDROID v0.682 numbers the packet ported (x1.5 and 0.005*mastery) are a different tuning.

new_findings.text: Complete web-build numbers for the Focus/reload meter. Max is a hard constant 8*24 = 192 frames (8 s at 24 fps), NOT 48 + 6*SPD — the getBaseReload() value is stored and never read. It fills +1 per tick, so a full bar takes exactly 8 s. Per-slash drain is the weapon's slashusage (floor 48) scaled by stance: /2 in Light, x1 in Balanced and Reversed, x1.5 in Heavy and Dual. Switching stance costs a flat 48 frames on the web (android cuts to a third above half, else minus a sixth). The Focus skill sets reload to maxreload - 1. And a stance switch is refused outright while reload < maxreload/6 — that is the 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' label visible in the longplay.

new_findings.text: The native canvas is 800x480 = 5:3 EXACTLY, as a literal in BOTH builds — so the pillarbox origin that claims 0 and 1 both left open is CLOSED without a build. A 5:3 stage fitted to 1080 px gives 1800 px of picture and 60 px bars; the frames measure 1814-1816 px and 52-53 px bars, i.e. the game's own 5:3 canvas plus ~0.9% recorder stretch. The bars are the GAME's canvas, not the recorder's window. Re-base HUD x as (x-52)/1816 then map onto an 800-wide stage.
new_findings.quote: public static var stageWidth:int = 800;  ·  public static var stageHeight:int = 480;  ·  public static var stageBaseWidth:int = 800;  ·  public static var stageBaseHeight:int = 480;   — and independently in the WEB payload's obfuscated StatsManager: public static var stageWidth:int = 800;

new_findings.lane_impact: L-ui-hud: blocker ① CLOSED outright and its close-path was wrong — it never needed a build, the literal is in the decompiled source of both builds. Confirms the ledger's own unsourced '800x480 (5:3)' line with an A2 cite.

new_findings.text: Kill-XP is HELD, closing the lead claim 21 opened. Every NPC gets xp = level*2 + 20 at init; bosses and duel opponents get xp = lvl*5 + 45. It was never in npcdata because it is computed in code.
new_findings.quote: NPC.as:218  this.xp = this.level * 2 + 20;   ·   NPC.as:252  this.xp = lvl * 2 + 20;   ·   EnemyPlayer.as:80-89  if(this.isBoss || this.isDuelist) { xp = lvl * 5 + 45; … } else { xp = lvl * 2 + 20; }

new_findings.lane_impact: L-progression blocker ④ ('full XP-income model') loses its kill-XP half outright; L-economy's '20+ samples show no XP formula either' is overturned.

new_findings.text: The boss HP/ATK derivation is real shipped code, which vindicates the max() reasoning that packet claim 20 says rests on a false premise. maxhp = max(levelScaledAuthoredHP, playerhit x hitsToKillBoss), and the same shape for attack.
new_findings.quote: :97 hitsToKillBoss = 8 + lvldiff;  :98 hitsToKillPlayer = 16 - lvldiff;  :107 playerhit = playerATK - defense;  :124 bossHP = playerhit * hitsToKillBoss;  :125 if(bossHP > maxhp) { maxhp = bossHP; setHP(maxhp); }  :131 bosshit = playerHP / hitsToKillPlayer;  :132 bossATK = bosshit + playerDEF;  :133 if(bossATK > minDamage) { minDamage = bossATK; }
new_findings.ledger_text: Damage math: Physical = (ATK + WeaponDMG) × stanceMult; Heavy defender Defense ×0.8 (one way); Critical = 1.3 × Physical.
new_findings.lane_impact: L-combat-core: the whole boss-scaling model is now codeable exactly — including the level-banded playerhit floors at :108-123 (lvl<=10 -> 1, <=20 -> L/8, <=30 -> L/6, else L/4). src/config/combat-sim.ts's comment needs one clause fixed ('not authored at all'), not a rewrite.

new_findings.text: Every enemy spawned with an explicit level <= 10 is FORCED to 1 HP / 1 damage / 1 defense regardless of authored values, and levels 11-20 are damped by x0.9. This is the mechanism behind the '~1-HP-chip field trash' the videos show.
